question: Find the chunk of background information in your scene and compost it: break it up, spread it out, and slip it into conversation or action-narration as implication, passing reference, or hint.

source.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
source.quote: As you write the scene, "compost" the information, break it up, spread it out, slip it into conversation or action-narration or anywhere you can make implication, by passing reference, by hint, by any means you like.

question: Make your scene understandable to a reader who has not read your background notes: include enough of the situation that it stands alone without them.

source.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
source.quote: You don't have to write the whole story; just a scene or two that is based on this information and includes enough of it to be understandable to a reader who has not read the information.

question: Choose something you know how to do that involves a complex series of specific actions — making bread, sailing a boat, repairing an engine — and build a scene around the process.

source.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
source.quote: Think of something you know how to do that involves a complex series of specific actions: for example; making a loaf of bread or a piece of jewelry, building a barn, playing a game of blackjack or a game of polo, sailing a boat, repairing an engine, setting up a conference, setting a broken wrist, setting type

question: Rewrite your scene so the process runs with at least two people present, either in the background of a conversation or as the locus of the action.

source.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
source.quote: Write a scene, involving at least two people; in which this process is going on, either in the background of a conversation, or as the locus of the action.

question: Make the steps of the process clear to the reader, but keep it in the background — the process should not appear to be what the piece is about.

source.author: Ursula K. Le Guin
source.quote: Whatever the process is, make the various steps clear to the reader, but don't let it appear to be what the piece is all about.
